title: Are Our Hearts Strong Enough to Get to Mars? - Nautilus
gist: A Circulation study suggests the cardiovascular toll of prolonged spaceflight, a key barrier to Mars missions lasting over a year, may be less stubborn than feared. The article gives the setup but not the study's findings.

insights.claim: A round trip to Mars would take over a year, and muscle atrophy in microgravity makes the heart especially vulnerable.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Physiological risk is a real constraint on crewed Mars timelines.
insights.locator: any voyage to the red planet and back will take over a year

insights.claim: A new Circulation study finds the cardiac hurdle of long spaceflight might not be as stubborn as thought.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Lowers a perceived blocker for crewed deep-space missions.
insights.locator: a new study published in the journal Circulation

insights.claim: Astronauts returning after even short stays in space often get dizzy spells caused partly by a sudden blood-pressure drop.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.locator: Humans returning to Earth after even minimal periods
